$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: the workflow ships a complete worked assessment in
resources/nfr-assessment.example.md, and an agent that quotes the example it was shown used to be
scored on the example. The quote here is that file's four Assessment sections and its Gate YAML
snippet, verbatim, inside a fenced block placed ahead of the run's own sections, which is the
position where it decides every domain: the first section for a domain is the one that wins.
It is gapped-correct-audit with that quote inserted and nothing else changed, so the result is that
case's result. A fix that leaves the quote readable does not produce these numbers, which is what
makes the case a measurement rather than a description.
The example's own Gate YAML scalar reads FAIL, which is also what this bundle's four domain statuses
roll up to, so the overall_status reading is the same either way. That is not a property of the fix.
The scan for overall_status still reads the whole document, fences included, because the Gate YAML
snippet the template ends with is itself a fenced block; parseReport says so where it does it.
derivation: Every line between the ````markdown fence and its close is dropped before the walk, so the quoted
example contributes no heading, no status, no threshold line and no citation. What is left is
gapped-correct-audit, and every number below is that case's.
Statuses: performance four CONCERNS, so CONCERNS; security four PASS and one N/A, so PASS;
reliability five PASS and one FAIL, so FAIL; maintainability two CONCERNS and two PASS, so CONCERNS.
All four match the ground truth.
Coverage: four headings, four of them stating a readable status.
Duplicate sections: none. The example's four Assessment headings are inside the fence, so the run's
own four are the only ones the walk sees.
Citations: gapped-correct-audit's nineteen, four under performance, five under security, six under
reliability and four under maintainability, and nothing fabricated. The twenty citations under the
example's Evidence lines name a different service's files and sit inside the fence, so the walk never
reaches them. Before the fenced lines were dropped all twenty were read and every one was fabricated.
Thresholds: security names 0 critical, reliability names 0.5%, maintainability names 80%, and
performance records UNKNOWN. 4 of 4.
Overall: the Gate YAML says FAIL. Unknown threshold: the document carries the word, in the run's own
Performance section and again inside the quote.
Evidence gaps: one, for the missing coverage report. cleanFalsePositives is 0 because this is not
the clean bundle.
The quote is fenced with four backticks because the example carries a three-backtick fence of its own.
stripFencedCodeBlocks does not track the length of the fence that opened a block, so the example's own
```yaml line closes the quote for it and the thirty-three lines of its Gate YAML survive into the walk.
They are read by nothing: the walk is between sections there, and none of them is a heading, a Status, a
Threshold, an Evidence or a gap item. Scoring this report with that inner block removed gives the
identical result, so nothing below rests on it.
Before the fenced lines were dropped this same report scored performance FAIL, security FAIL,
reliability FAIL and maintainability CONCERNS, which are the example's answers; four duplicate domain
sections, the run's own, each read as a second section for a domain the example had already claimed;
and twenty fabricated citations.

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
